Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring a study of the incidence of total permanent disability pensions in the state's workers' compensation system.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a study of the incidence of total permanentdisability pensions in the state's workers' compensation system; andcreating new sections.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The department of labor and industriesshall conduct a study of the incidence of total permanent disabilitypensions in the state's workers' compensation system. The departmentshall contract with an independent researcher approved by the labor andbusiness members of the workers' compensation advisory committee. Theindependent researcher must have demonstrated expertise in workers'compensation systems. The department shall consult with the workers'compensation advisory committee in determining the criteria to use inselecting a researcher and in selecting the researcher with which tocontract. (2) In conducting the study under subsection (1) of this section,the researcher selected shall consider the following: (a) Causes of the recent increase in total permanent disabilitycases, including changes in injured worker demographics, policy, andother areas that may be identified; p. 1 SHB 1792 (b) Future anticipated total permanent disability trends; (c) A comparison of Washington's permanent disability claimsexperience and injured workers with other states and jurisdictions; (d) The impact of the standard for finding workers employable onthe incidence of permanent total disability pensions; and (e) The impact of vocational rehabilitation under RCW 51.32.095,and any improvements to vocational rehabilitation, on the incidence ofpermanent total disability pensions. (3) The department shall report to the workers' compensationadvisory committee on the results of the study on or before July 1,2008.
If specific funding for the purposes of thisact, referencing this act by bill or chapter number, is not provided byJune 30, 2007, in the omnibus appropriations act, this act is null andvoid.
